text:
elaine: FYI reproducible ordering bug when reconnecting Node SSE client through proxy — later chunks arrive before earlier ones.
sam: repro steps?
elaine: start a long stream (~1500 tokens), kill the client (SIGINT), reconnect immediately. Node emits seq 10 then seq 7.
kyle: do we have proxy/runtime logs?
elaine: runtime tcp shows 7,8,9,10. Proxy delivered 10 then 7. Suspect proxy handoff mixes buffers.
sam: could auth refresh be opening a second backend connection?
elaine: yes — AuthRelay refresh opens a new backend while draining old one. That matches merging behaviour.
kyle: short-term mitigations: (1) SDK debounce reconnects (200ms) and allow only one in-flight resume per stream id, (2) proxy should not merge inflight backend buffers; force drain or advertise resume token.
sam: add seq inside data payload as guard: data: {"seq":42,...} so clients can reorder/detect dupes.
elaine: Node SDK action: replace current parser with a minimal stateful SSE parser that waits for full event terminator (

) before emitting. Also add reconnect debounce.
elaine: filed bug ENG-STREAM-1140 with logs and tcp dump. infra-bot: scheduled proxy audit INFRA-734.
kyle: Default UX: try one resume then fail with clear code. Provide fail_fast opt-in.
sam: add a devex sample that forces token expiry and asserts monotonic seq consumption.
elaine: I'll open a small PR for Node with parser + debounce and a sample harness.
elaine: PR link (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/492
sam: thanks — infra, please confirm whether proxy handoff is the root cause before we ship server-side changes.
